name: get_document_history
description: List the saved git history for a session (newest first, read-only: never mutates, never flips dirty). Paginate with limit (1-100, default 20) and offset (default 0). Returns {ok:true,sessionId,documentPath,currentCommit,totalCommits,history:[{oid,message,author,timestamp,timestampMs,opCount,affectedNodeIds,resultingHeadOid}]} (timestampMs = ms-precision epoch millis; commit-time clock for tracked commits, git seconds for older ones; opCount is always present (0 for pre-tracking commits and heals-only saves: it folds operations, not normalizer rewrites); affectedNodeIds is always present ([] when untracked); resultingHeadOid always equals oid (append-only; refs never move). Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","limit":10} -> history slice. Use the oids with revert_document (or preview_revert first) to restore an earlier saved state. IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions, and duplicate client-supplied ids are rejected. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.
